# The module-drain probe corpus (PARITY MD1) — ONE set of bytes, served to BOTH engines.
#
# Chrome 150.0.7871.46 was asked for it over the delaying server below and its answer is
# `module-drain-probe.chrome-150.txt`; `module_drain_live.rs` serves this same file from a
# `TcpListener` that applies the SAME delays and asserts korvus prints the same lines. The two
# drivers share these bytes rather than two copies of them.
#
# FORMAT. One file per `=== <path> <content-type>` header; the body is every line up to the next
# header, verbatim. Lines beginning `#` BEFORE the first header are this comment; after it they are
# body.
#
# THE DELAY IS IN THE PATH, and both servers derive it the same way: a path whose first segment is
# `d<milliseconds>` is answered that many milliseconds late, and a path whose first segment is
# `hang` is never answered at all. `/d700/dep1.mjs` is served 700 ms after the request arrives.
# Nothing else about the response changes. This is what makes the probe a measurement of a WAIT
# rather than of a parse: the bodies are one line each and the wall clock is entirely the server's.
#
# THE ORIGIN APPEARS NOWHERE IN THE TRANSCRIPT: every page imports by absolute path, so there is no
# port to normalize and the two drivers compare byte for byte.
#
# RE-RECORD (an idle box; Chrome's answer was identical on two runs, and two runs is the standard):
#
#   1. Lay this file out as a directory -- for each `=== <path> <ctype>` header, write the lines up
#      to the next header to `<dir>/<path>`.
#   2. Run the delaying server over that directory:
#
#        python3 - <dir> <<'EOF'
#        import http.server, os, re, socketserver, sys, time
#        ROOT, PORT = sys.argv[1], 8932
#        TYPES = {".html": "text/html", ".mjs": "text/javascript"}
#        class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
#            protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
#            def log_message(self, *a): pass
#            def do_GET(self):
#                p = self.path.split("?")[0]
#                if p.startswith("/hang/"):
#                    time.sleep(3600); return
#                m = re.match(r"^/d(\d+)/", p)
#                if m: time.sleep(int(m.group(1)) / 1000.0)
#                f = os.path.join(ROOT, p.lstrip("/"))
#                if not os.path.isfile(f):
#                    self.send_response(404); self.send_header("Content-Length", "0"); self.end_headers(); return
#                b = open(f, "rb").read()
#                self.send_response(200)
#                self.send_header("Content-Type", TYPES.get(os.path.splitext(f)[1], "text/plain"))
#                self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(b)))
#                self.send_header("Cache-Control", "no-store")
#                self.end_headers(); self.wfile.write(b)
#        class S(socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer): daemon_threads = True; allow_reuse_address = True
#        S(("127.0.0.1", PORT), H).serve_forever()
#        EOF
#
#   3. For each of `/index.html`, `/three.html`, `/chain.html`, in that order:
#      `google-chrome --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --user-data-dir=$(mktemp -d)
#       --virtual-time-budget=30000 --dump-dom http://127.0.0.1:8932/<page>`
#   4. Take the text of `<pre id="out">` from each and write it to
#      `module-drain-probe.chrome-150.txt`, each page's block preceded by a `== <page>` line.
#      Repeat step 3 and diff the two recordings before committing.
#
# THE FOUR PAGES THAT ARE MEASURED BUT NOT ASSERTED (`/long5.html`, `/six5.html`, `/long30.html`,
# `/hang.html`) are recorded in `module_drain_live.rs`'s module doc comment with their Chrome
# readings and their korvus readings side by side. They are laid out and served by the same two
# steps above; they are not in the compared transcript because korvus keeps a bounded drain and
# Chrome, measured here, bounds this nowhere.

=== /index.html text/html
<!doctype html>
<meta charset=utf-8>
<title>module drain probe — six modules, one 700 ms import each</title>
<pre id="out"></pre>
<script>
window.L = [];
window.P = function (s) { window.L.push(s); };
window.addEventListener('error', function () { P('error'); });
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { P('dcl'); });
window.addEventListener('load', function () {
  P('load');
  document.getElementById('out').textContent = window.L.join('\n');
});
</script>
<script type="module">import { n } from '/d700/dep1.mjs'; P('ran m1 dep=' + n);</script>
<script type="module">import { n } from '/d700/dep2.mjs'; P('ran m2 dep=' + n);</script>
<script type="module">import { n } from '/d700/dep3.mjs'; P('ran m3 dep=' + n);</script>
<script type="module">import { n } from '/d700/dep4.mjs'; P('ran m4 dep=' + n);</script>
<script type="module">import { n } from '/d700/dep5.mjs'; P('ran m5 dep=' + n);</script>
<script type="module">import { n } from '/d700/dep6.mjs'; P('ran m6 dep=' + n);</script>

=== /hang.html text/html
<!doctype html>
<meta charset=utf-8>
<title>module drain probe — one module whose import never answers</title>
<pre id="out"></pre>
<script>
window.L = [];
window.P = function (s) { window.L.push(s); };
window.addEventListener('error', function () { P('error'); });
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { P('dcl'); document.title = 'saw dcl'; });
window.addEventListener('load', function () {
  P('load');
  document.title = 'saw load';
  document.getElementById('out').textContent = window.L.join('\n');
});
</script>
<script type="module">import { n } from '/hang/never.mjs'; P('ran hang dep=' + n);</script>
